Overview of ICCR scholarships and the selection timeline

summary: ICCR scholarships are offered by the Indian Council for Cultural Relations, Government of India, to foreign students who want to study in India at undergraduate, postgraduate or PhD level, or take a certificate or diploma in Indian languages, performing or visual arts or yoga. Students apply on the ICCR A2A portal, choose up to five university and course options at institutions empanelled with ICCR, and are selected by the Indian Mission in their country after a university has given provisional admission. The award pays a monthly stipend, a house rent allowance and other allowances, plus the admissible university charges, with a return air ticket after the course is completed.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants apply through the A2A portal and are selected by the Indian Mission in their own country. The guidelines do not print a list of countries, so availability depends on the Mission. Selection is at the sole discretion of the Mission, which can accept or reject any application at any stage without giving a reason. Admission by a university does not guarantee a scholarship.

Passport: valid for at least two years as on 1 July 2026.

PIO or OCI holders: they must have finished school (up to Standard XII) outside India and must not have studied in India in the preceding five academic years for PhD courses, or three years for PG courses.

Language: classes for foreign students are in English. Applicants must meet the English proficiency standard set by the Indian Mission and must submit a 500-word English essay on one of the topics listed on the portal. A TOEFL, IELTS or similar score can be uploaded as proof. A GMAT score is mandatory at some institutions for MBA courses.

Subject background: applicants for science and engineering UG courses must have studied Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry at Standard XII; those aiming at science courses with Biology as a major must have studied Biology, Physics and Chemistry.

PhD: admission to research courses is only at PhD level, with a synopsis of the research topic. The topic should not involve data collection in the home country or any other country outside India, as far as possible.

Performing arts: applicants upload a recent video or video link of their performance.

Current students: candidates already studying UG or PG in India must apply afresh on the portal. Only one application per academic year is allowed; multiple registrations lead to rejection.

Health: students must be in sound physical and mental health, free of chronic contagious or non-communicable disease, and have the required vaccinations. They must hold health insurance (see benefits). Students may not take paid part-time or full-time work while on the scholarship.

Equivalence: where an Equivalence Certificate from the Association of Indian Universities is a precondition, the Mission guides the student and the student pays the fee.

Falsifying the date of birth leads to automatic rejection or termination, a refund of all costs, and possible legal action.
age_experience_notes: Age is counted as on 1 July 2026. The guidelines set a minimum of 18 years for all levels; a maximum of 35 for UG, PG, certificate and diploma courses; a maximum of 40 for PhD. There is no upper age limit for Hindi, Sanskrit and Indian performing arts courses (for example Kathak, Bharatnatyam, vocal or instrumental music) unless the institution sets one. Institutions have their own age criteria on top of these. The Tokyo and Wellington pages print higher maximums (40 for UG, PG and diploma; 50 for PhD); the guidelines document is used here. No work experience requirement is stated.
funding_summary: The student receives a monthly stipend (UG INR 18,000; PG INR 20,000; PhD INR 22,000), a house rent allowance, an annual contingent allowance and, where a thesis or project report is required, a one-time thesis allowance. The guidelines say the student is entitled to the allowances and the admissible university charges for the length of the course, as long as the student is promoted each year. The allowances continue for the prescribed course length, or until the final result is declared if the student stays in India after the final exam, with up to 21 more days of allowances after the result to finish departure formalities. Regular PhD tenure is 3 years. A return air ticket is given only after the course is completed. Hostel and mess charges, health insurance and arrival costs are paid by the student.
programmes_note: Scholarships are only for structured courses of one year or longer at UG, PG and PhD level, and for certificate or diploma courses only in Indian languages and literature, performing or visual arts, and yoga. No scholarship is given for short-term certificates, diplomas or research courses other than PhD. No scholarships for medical science; paramedical courses such as nursing, physiotherapy, anaesthesia and lab technician; law; or 5-year integrated courses such as BA LLB or BSc plus MSc. No foreign admission to B.Tech courses at the IITs. Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy courses at UG, PG and PhD level run under the separate AYUSH Scholarship Scheme, which students can apply to only after the Mission announces it. Applicants choose up to five university and course combinations in order of priority; changing the course or university after the award is not allowed under any circumstances. Programmes are listed on the A2A portal per university.
institutions_note: Only universities and institutions empanelled with ICCR take part; the Wellington page and Tokyo notice mention 131 or more. Applicants pick up to five in order of priority. Admission to a course is the sole decision of the university; ICCR and the Mission have no role in it. Universities put provisional admission confirmations on the A2A portal, and the Mission then selects from those confirmations.

summary.detail: Undergraduate structured courses of one year or more at ICCR-empanelled institutions, taught in English. Science and engineering courses need Maths, Physics and Chemistry (or Biology, Physics and Chemistry) at Standard XII. Stipend INR 18,000 per month; house rent allowance INR 6,500 (Grade I cities) or INR 5,500 (other cities); contingent allowance INR 5,000 a year; thesis allowance INR 7,000 only where a project report is required. Age 18 to 35 on 1 July 2026.

Postgraduate structured courses of one year or more at ICCR-empanelled institutions, taught in English. Stipend INR 20,000 per month; contingent allowance INR 7,000 a year; thesis allowance INR 7,000 only where a project report is required. GMAT is mandatory for MBA at some institutions. Age 18 to 35 on 1 July 2026.

PhD at ICCR-empanelled institutions. A research synopsis is required, and the topic should not need data collection outside India. Stipend INR 22,000 per month; contingent allowance INR 12,500 a year; thesis allowance INR 10,000. Regular tenure is 3 years; extensions are at ICCR's sole discretion, up to six months at a time and a maximum of two years, and no stipend is paid for a viva-voce extension. Age 18 to 40 on 1 July 2026.
summary.source_text: Scholarship Allowances; Prescribed tenure of scholarship for a regular Ph.D. student

summary.detail: Certificate or diploma courses of one year or more, offered only in Indian languages and literature, performing or visual arts, and yoga. Maximum age 35 on 1 July 2026, with no upper limit for Hindi, Sanskrit and Indian performing arts courses unless the institution sets one. The stipend table in the guidelines does not list a separate row for certificate or diploma courses.

benefits.limit_text: Admissible charges of the university or institution for the duration of the course
benefits.conditions: Subject to regular promotion each year. No tuition or other fees are paid for a repeat year. A Tokyo embassy notice lists tuition fee among the covered items; the guidelines do not itemise the fees.

benefits.limit_text: Monthly stipend: UG INR 18,000; PG INR 20,000; PhD INR 22,000
benefits.conditions: Paid only by bank transfer, after joining formalities and a bank account at a State Bank of India branch are done (this takes about 2 to 3 months). Paid on academic progress. Half the stipend is deducted for a continuous stay outside India of 31 to 60 days; stays outside India are limited to 60 paid days a year and two trips a year. Stipend stops while dues to the university are unpaid or semester progress reports are not sent.

benefits.limit_text: House rent allowance of INR 6,500 per month (Grade I cities) or INR 5,500 per month (other cities)
benefits.conditions: The guidelines table prints the rent allowance once, against the UG row. The student pays hostel or private accommodation charges directly. A student who takes a hostel place may not leave it before the end of the academic year.

benefits.limit_text: Annual contingent allowance: UG INR 5,000; PG INR 7,000; PhD INR 12,500
One-time thesis or dissertation allowance: UG INR 7,000; PG INR 7,000; PhD INR 10,000
benefits.conditions: For UG and PG only where a project report is required by the course.

benefits.limit_text: Return air ticket to the home country after the course is completed
benefits.conditions: Given only on successful completion, not to students who leave early. Request it at least 15 days before travel with the required papers. Airfare and travel costs to India, visa-related costs at arrival, and excess baggage are not paid unless the scheme says so.

benefits.limit_text: Student buys health insurance with cover of at least INR 500,000 at own cost
benefits.conditions: Mandatory before allowances are paid. It can be bought at home if valid in India, or in India after joining. All illness costs are the student's responsibility.

benefits.limit_text: Hostel and mess charges, AIU Equivalence Certificate fees, immigration (FRRO) registration fees and penalties, and the cost of initial settlement
benefits.conditions: The guidelines advise bringing about USD 1,500 for initial settlement, because allowances start only after joining formalities are complete.

requirements.text: Passport valid for at least two years as on 1 July 2026.

Academic certificates and transcripts from school onwards, certified and translated into English. Originals, with a notarised English translation where the document is in another language, are taken to India and checked by the university. Bring a certified copy of the transcript or syllabus of the last qualifying exam (high school for UG, UG for PG, Master's for PhD).
Passport-size photograph on a white background with both ears visible, as specified on the portal.
Essay of 500 words in English on one of the topics listed on the portal.
TOEFL, IELTS or similar English test certificate or score (optional proof of English; the Mission decides how English proficiency is judged).
Synopsis of the research topic. The topic should not involve data collection outside India, as far as possible.
Video or video link of a recent performance.

requirements.conditional_rule: Applicants to MBA courses at institutions that require it

requirements.text: Equivalence Certificate of the Association of Indian Universities, obtained with guidance from the Indian Mission, at the student's cost.
requirements.conditional_rule: Where the university or course requires it

requirements.text: Medical fitness certificate with test reports and vaccinations, issued by a reputed hospital or laboratory (or as the Mission prescribes), uploaded after selection within the time limit given.

To bring to India: offer letter from the Mission, medical fitness certificate, English proficiency certificates if any, PhD synopsis, AIU certificate if applicable, Joining Report form from the portal, extra passport photographs, and any other document the university needs.

application_steps.title: Register and apply on the ICCR A2A portal
application_steps.detail: Apply online only on the A2A scholarship portal; applications sent to a Mission, ICCR or a university by any other route are not accepted. Make only one application per academic year. Enter data exactly and upload the documents as the portal specifies; any mismatch can lead to cancellation. Students already studying UG or PG in India must apply afresh.

application_steps.title: Choose up to five university and course options
application_steps.detail: Pick from institutions empanelled with ICCR, in order of priority. Check subject, age and English requirements first. Changing course or university after the award is not allowed.

application_steps.title: Write the essay and add course-specific items
application_steps.detail: Write the 500-word essay in English. PhD applicants add a research synopsis, performing arts applicants add a performance video, and MBA applicants check whether GMAT is required. A TOEFL or IELTS score may be uploaded.

application_steps.title: University decides on admission
application_steps.detail: Each university decides on admission on its own and uploads a provisional admission confirmation on the A2A portal. ICCR and the Mission have no say in admission. In the 2026-27 round, Budapest and Buenos Aires embassy pages show different dates for the university and mission stages, so timing depends on the country.

application_steps.title: Indian Mission selects candidates
application_steps.detail: After the admission stage the Indian Mission in the applicant's country judges candidates on several criteria. Admission does not guarantee an award, and the Mission can reject any candidate at any stage. A second round lets Missions issue offers for unused slots from a reserve list.

application_steps.title: Accept the offer and upload medical fitness
application_steps.detail: The Mission issues an offer letter. Accept or reject it on the portal within 7 days, and upload the medical fitness certificate within the time limit. If you do not reply in time, the award is cancelled.

application_steps.title: Get the visa and register for the SII portal
application_steps.detail: Create a unique ID on the SII portal, which is required for the visa. UG, PG, certificate and diploma students get a Student Visa (S-1); PhD students get a Research Visa (S-5). Check the visa details and upload them on the A2A portal. Join within the date in the offer; joining later is not permitted. Upload travel details, preferably 15 to 20 days before arrival.

application_steps.title: Arrive, register and join the course
application_steps.detail: Report to the university's international centre and the ICCR zonal or sub-zonal office on the day of arrival or the next day. Register with the immigration authorities (FRRO) within 14 days. Admission is provisional until the university checks your original documents. Fill in the Joining Report, which ICCR needs before releasing allowances. Open a State Bank of India account and buy the required health insurance.

application_steps.title: Keep up academic progress and rules
application_steps.detail: Allowances depend on promotion each year, regular attendance and semester progress reports. Failing a year suspends the award and the repeat year is self-financed; failing again ends it. No paid work, no political activity or protests, and no social media content that harms India or relations with the home country; breaches can end the scholarship. Stays outside India need prior university permission and are limited to 60 paid days a year.

application_steps.title: Return home after the course
application_steps.detail: Leave India after the final result, with no more than two months between finishing and leaving. Request the return air ticket at least 15 days before travel, with passport, visa, residence permit, completion certificate, no-dues certificate, alumni portal registration and exit permit. Register on the alumni portal and close the bank account before leaving.

not_stated: Which countries are eligible (the guidelines print no list; the Mission decides)
How the Mission weighs candidates; no scoring criteria are given
Minimum English test scores (the Mission sets the standard)
Application closing time and a single global closing date (dates differ by Mission and the pages seen disagree)
Number of awards per country or overall for this year
List of empanelled universities and their courses (these are on the A2A portal only)
Whether the house rent allowance applies to PG and PhD students (the table prints it once, on the UG row)
Stipend for certificate and diploma courses
Exact list of tuition and other fees ICCR pays to the university
fetch_problems: The ICCR A2A portal and the ICCR site itself were not opened; the guidelines were read from copies hosted by the Indian Embassy in Djibouti and the Consulate General in Sao Paulo.
The Hague and Wellington pages carry only summary text and refer to the guidelines PDF; Wellington's slots-and-schemes list PDF was not reachable.
notes: Source pages disagree on maximum ages: guidelines say 35 (UG, PG, certificate, diploma) and 40 (PhD); the Tokyo and Wellington pages say 40 and 50. The guidelines are used.

Source pages disagree on the application opening date: Tokyo says 23 February 2026, Wellington and Budapest say 27 February 2026, Buenos Aires says 7 February 2026. Closing dates also differ by Mission (Budapest: 27 May 2026; Buenos Aires: 15 April 2026).

The Tokyo embassy notice says the award covers tuition, living allowances, housing and airfare; this wording is not used because the guidelines say airfare to India is not covered and hostel, mess and insurance are paid by the student.
The Wellington page and the Buenos Aires page show a last-updated date of 11 November 2026, so their dates may have been revised.
